topic: why prefill cannot reach parity on this toolchain (op-count accounting)

vector_ops_per_64_elements.pass2: vld + vcvt + vld(w f32) + vmul + vmul + vcvt(bf16) + vsts = 7

analysis.per_core_instruction_estimate: 8192 rows * 4096 elements * (10/64) / 64 cores = ~82,000 vector instructions per core; at ~1 per cycle and ~1.8 GHz this is already ~45 us of pure issue, consistent with the observed ~90 us vec-busy time
analysis.vendor_estimate: if the vendor fuses bf16 load with an fp32 multiply-accumulate (implicit conversion), each pass is 2 ops instead of 3 and the scale pass ~4 instead of 7, giving ~6 per 64 elements -> ~49 us, consistent with its measured 50-72 us

toolchain_gap: no implicit bf16->fp32 conversion in vld (vld never converts)
no bf16 multiply-accumulate into an fp32 accumulator (vmula with bf16 operands is rejected)
cube/matmul codegen is incompatible with the installed CANN (only 9.1 and 9.2 exist; the generated asc_* cube APIs are absent; the official example_gemm.py fails identically)
conclusion: prefill parity requires a TileLang/CANN capability this machine does not have. The 0.62x result is not a tuning shortfall; it is the op-count ceiling of the available instruction set.
not_proven: nothing here changes the decode result; no acceptance has completed yet
